stories.title: Europe’s AI labeling and transparency rules are now in effect
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: The EU's AI Act now mandates transparency regarding AI interactions.
Companies must disclose when users are interacting with AI models like chatbots.
The rules also require labeling of AI-generated content, such as deepfakes.

stories.title: US company’s AI lets Ukraine’s cheap kamikaze drones track targets on their own
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: A US company is providing advanced AI capabilities to Ukraine's inexpensive kamikaze drones.
The deal involves equipping 50,000 Ukrainian drones with US-developed autonomous tracking AI.
The transaction is valued at $100 million, highlighting significant military tech transfer.

stories.title: Structured Memory for Edge Language Models: Persistent Context and Corpus Retrieval via O(1) SSM State Injection
stories.author: Jonathan Tapson
bullet_points: Introduces PRECOG, a novel retrieval mechanism designed to enhance Edge Language Models.
Addresses the high prefill cost ($O(L_{context})$) associated with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by collapsing it to $O(1)$ per query.
Leverages the inherent properties of State-Space Models (SSMs) to manage persistent context efficiently, bypassing traditional KV-cache growth issues.

stories.title: Show HN: Run an 80B Qwen in 4.3 GB of RAM on a Mac, and a 35B on an iPhone
stories.author: leonickson
bullet_points: Demonstrates extreme efficiency in running large language models (LLMs) locally.
Achieves significant memory reduction, running an 80B parameter model on only 4.3 GB of RAM on a Mac.
Highlights the feasibility of running powerful models on consumer-grade, resource-constrained devices like iPhones.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is currently serving a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Coding agent tasks show up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The updated engine also delivers faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is its local-first architecture, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing local AI inference.
This is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and speed.
The core value proposition is bringing powerful AI capabilities directly onto the user's own hardware.

stories.title: Microsoft is bringing Xbox 360 games to PC
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is expanding its PC gaming initiative to include Xbox 360 titles.
The move follows the prior announcement of bringing original Xbox games to PC.
The plan allows developers to port their Xbox 360 games to run on next-gen PCs.

stories.title: Structured Memory for Edge Language Models: Persistent Context and Corpus Retrieval via O(1) SSM State Injection
stories.author: Jonathan Tapson
bullet_points: Introduces PRECOG, a novel retrieval mechanism designed for Edge Language Models.
Addresses the high prefill cost ($O(L_{context})$) associated with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by achieving $O(1)$ prefill.
Leverages the inherent properties of State-Space Models (SSMs) to manage persistent context efficiently, bypassing the growing KV-cache issue of Transformers.

stories.title: Magnet: Detecting Cross-Session AI Misuse Through Capability Accumulation
stories.author: Matthew Dressman
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical gap in AI safety by focusing on cross-session misuse, moving beyond single-session threat models.
It highlights that modern, powerful AI systems are increasingly composed of coordinated ensembles of specialized agents, not just single models.
This ensemble architecture introduces new, complex risks that current abuse detection frameworks are ill-equipped to handle.

stories.title: MedPRESS: A Multi-turn Benchmark for Patient-Pressure-Induced Medical Sycophancy in LLMs
stories.author: Niloy Farhan
bullet_points: Introduces MedPRESS, a new multi-turn benchmark specifically designed to test LLMs in realistic, patient-facing medical conversations.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM safety research by moving beyond static questions to measure 'patient-pressure-induced sycophancy'.
Comprises 600 medically grounded dialogues across scenarios like medication demand, self-care, and symptom triage.

stories.title: Cultural Awareness is Represented but Not Decoded: Tracing Mythological Knowledge across 18 Open-Source LLMs
stories.author: Mika Hämäläinen
bullet_points: The study investigates how cultural knowledge is encoded in 18 open-source Large Language Models (LLMs).
LLMs show strong recall for major Western deities (Zeus, Jupiter, Thor) but struggle significantly with less-represented mythological figures.
Researchers use advanced interpretability techniques (linear probing, activation patching) to trace where this cultural bias originates within the model architecture.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance Claude Code's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Palworld’s expanding to mobile with a new MMORPG
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Palworld is expanding its reach to mobile platforms (iOS and Android).
The mobile version will be a new open-world MMORPG, titled Palworld Online.
Garena is developing the new title, aiming to reimagine the original PC game's depth for mobile.

stories.title: An AI-supervised remote exam went so badly that 58,000 students must retake it
stories.author: Nate Anderson
bullet_points: An AI-supervised remote examination system experienced significant failure.
The system's performance was flawed, leading to an increase in top scores by fivefold.
Consequently, 58,000 students were required to retake the examination.

stories.title: Bridging Artificial Intelligence and Power Systems Education Using a Hands-On Executable Framework
stories.author: Li
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap between advanced AI applications in power systems and the lack of reusable educational tools for newcomers.
It proposes the concept of Engineering-Grounded AI (EGAI) to integrate AI workflows with established power system engineering practices.
The work introduces a hands-on, executable framework designed to bridge the gap between AI theory and practical power system education.

stories.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings
stories.author: Shu Wu
bullet_points: Introduces UEmbed, a new unified embedding model designed for multimodal tasks.
Addresses limitations in existing Learned Sparse Retrieval (LSR) methods, which are often tied to encoder-style architectures.
Aims to improve multimodal retrieval by moving beyond reliance on auxiliary cross-modal modules using a decoder-only approach.

stories.title: AtumAI: A Principled Framework for Agentic Generation of Datacenter Control-Plane Policies
stories.author: Jovan Stojkovic
bullet_points: The paper introduces AtumAI, a framework designed to automate the complex design of datacenter control-plane policies.
The challenge addressed is the growing complexity and vast design space of modern hardware-software datacenter stacks.
The framework aims to overcome limitations in off-the-shelf agentic AI by providing a formal and structured approach to policy generation.

stories.title: A Taxonomy of Cognitive Capability Gaps in Generative and Agentic AI
stories.author: Shahram Rahimi
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitations of current Generative and Agentic AI, which often lack sustained reasoning and adaptive behavior.
It proposes a taxonomy to categorize the 'cognitive capability gaps' in existing AI systems.
The goal of Cognitive AI is to move beyond simple task execution toward systems with persistent memory and self-regulation.

stories.title: Who Should Be Generated? Justifying Demographic Targets in Open-Ended Generation
stories.author: Wenqing Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of justifying demographic targets in open-ended AI generation.
Current fairness evaluations often focus only on model output composition without establishing what the 'correct' composition should be.
It highlights the gap between input-side fairness definitions and output-side auditing practices in generative models.

stories.title: onepot-Bench 0: towards lab-aware in silico chemistry benchmarks
stories.author: Daniil A. Boiko
bullet_points: Language models are increasingly used in laboratory science for tasks like experiment planning and analysis.
Current evaluations struggle to accurately measure scientific capabilities because they require both problem-solving and domain intuition.
The paper introduces 'onepot-Bench' to create benchmarks that specifically test lab-aware decision-making, moving beyond reliance on public datasets.

stories.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
stories.author: Zilong Zheng
bullet_points: Introduces GradCuit, a method to improve LLM outputs via optimization-based latent reasoning at test time.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods where latent state updates are indirectly linked to reasoning via decoded tokens.
GradCuit directly inserts optimizable latent states to enable robust and interpretable credit assignment for latent updates.

stories.title: Pseudorandom Streams within Diffusion Models Act as Learnable Inputs That Affect Generation Quality
stories.author: Yanze Guo
bullet_points: Diffusion models' stochastic inputs are effectively deterministic numerical orbits on finite-precision hardware.
The structure of these accessible pseudorandom orbits can be treated as a learnable input influencing model training and generation quality.
A small MLP can be used to predict the next state of these orbits based on their recent history.

stories.title: AURORA-LM: Autoencoding Unified Representation for Continuous-Latent Diffusion Language Modeling
stories.author: Chenyang Si
bullet_points: AURORA-LM proposes a novel approach to bridge the gap between continuous latent space modeling (used for images/video) and discrete token-based language modeling.
The model addresses the fidelity loss in existing continuous language models by preserving a high-capacity representation instead of simplifying it for diffusion.
This research tackles a key limitation in generative AI, where text generation remains predominantly discrete despite advancements in continuous modeling for other modalities.

stories.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
stories.author: Zilong Zheng
bullet_points: Introduces GradCuit, a method for optimizing instance-specific latent states in LLMs at test time without altering model parameters.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods where credit assignment for latent updates is indirect, obscuring how latent states influence reasoning.
Uses 'gradient through circuit' to enable direct and interpretable credit assignment for latent reasoning within LLMs.

stories.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings
stories.author: Shu Wu
bullet_points: Introduces UEmbed, a new unified embedding framework for multimodal tasks.
Addresses limitations in existing Learned Sparse Retrieval (LSR) by moving beyond encoder-style bidirectional architectures.
Aims to simplify multimodal embedding by integrating sparse and dense representations within a decoder-only structure.

stories.title: Who Should Be Generated? Justifying Demographic Targets in Open-Ended Generation
stories.author: Wenqing Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of justifying demographic targets in open-ended generative AI outputs.
It highlights a gap in current fairness evaluations, which often assume sensitive attributes are provided in the input prompt.
The research focuses on output-side demographic composition audits, questioning the arbitrary nature of the targets used for comparison.

stories.title: LiveMem: Maintaining Memory State Continuity in Long-Running LLM Inference
stories.author: Yang Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of maintaining persistent state in long-running LLM inference where context windows are finite.
Introduces the concept of 'state continuity under context turnover' to manage computation across memory state changes.
Proposes 'LiveMem' as a method to carry forward computation independent of the active context size.

stories.title: SWE-Touch: Benchmarking Coding Agents When Users Touch the Code
stories.author: Kang Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SWE-Touch, a new framework to benchmark coding agents in real-world, shared development environments.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks by testing how agents handle code modifications made by human users during an active task.
Uses 'Counter-Edits' to simulate plausible user interventions, stress-testing the agent's ability to understand and respond to external code changes.

stories.title: I made my website callable by another AI agent — here's the actual JSON-RPC
stories.author: andriy_pyvovarchuk
bullet_points: The article discusses enabling direct communication between AI agents (A2A) rather than relying on human intervention.
It focuses on implementing a JSON-RPC interface to allow one AI agent to call another's website/API.
This represents a shift from traditional AI integration methods that require manual client development.
